sections.text:
1 Haec formula auctoris, ni fallimur, christiani (v. 15, Ναζωραῖος) nomina ange-
lorum et daemonum continet plerumque corrupta, quae iam is qui scripsit inter-
pretari non posset. Ista verborum nos commonent Hieronymi (Epist. 75, t. I,
col. 687, Migne, P.L.) : Armagil, Barbelon, Abraxas, Balsamum, et ridiculum
Leusiboram ceteraque magis portenta quam nomina, quae ad imperitorum et
muliercularum animos concitandos quasi de Hebraicis fontibus hauriunt, barbaro
simplices quosque terrentes tono ; ut quod non intelligunt plus mirentur. [F. C.] —
Formulam magicam eiusdem farinae edidimus in Catal. Mediol., p. 53.
sections.en:
1 This formula of a Christian author, unless we are mistaken (v. 15, Nazorean), contains names of angels
and demons mostly corrupt, which already he who wrote could not
interpret. Those words remind us of Jerome (Epist. 75, t. I,
col. 687, Migne, P.L.) : Armagil, Barbelon, Abraxas, Balsamum, and the ridiculous
Leusibora and other monsters rather than names, which they draw as if from Hebrew sources to
excite the minds of the ignorant and of little women, terrifying
all the simple with a barbarous tone; so that what they do not understand they may marvel at more. [F. C.] —
We have published a magic formula of the same flour in Catal. Mediol., p. 53.

summary.headline: Bowl-Divination Ritual
summary.text: A bowl-divination ritual from folio 233: a new bowl is placed at an old crossroads, followed by a midnight rite on a black horse and an invocation of demons associated with the west, Aries, and Hades. The formula invokes names including Xerion, Ariel, Saraphael, Berzebouel, Semiramel, Sabaoth, and Nazorean; the commentary identifies it as Christian and compares it with Jerome’s discussion of corrupted angelic and demonic names.
